original: Section 1.  Termination for Casualty.  If the Leased Premises are damaged or destroyed by fire or other casualty, Base Rent and Additional Rent shall abate in full of the date of such damage until the Leased Premises are restored and Tenant is able to resume normal production operations. Landlord shall, within thirty (30) days after the casualty, deliver to Tenant Landlord’s good-faith estimate of the time required to complete restoration. Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice given at any time before substantial completion if (a) Landlord’s restoration estimate exceeds ninety (90) days from the date of casualty, (b) the cost to restore exceeds ten percent (10%) of the replacement cost of the Leased Premises, (c) restoration is not substantially completed within thirty (30) days after the estimated completion date, or (d) the casualty occurs during the final twenty-four (24) months of the then-current Term. Upon any such termination, any unearned rent paid in advance shall be refunded and the Security Deposit returned in full. Landlord shall have no right to terminate this Lease by reason of casualty.
revised: Section 1.  Termination for Casualty.  If the Leased Premises are damaged or destroyed by fire or other casualty, Base Rent and Additional Rent shall abate in proportion to the portion of the Leased Premises rendered unusable for the Permitted Use, from the date of such damage until the Leased Premises are restored, and shall abate in full only for so long as the whole of the Leased Premises is unusable for the Permitted Use. Landlord shall, within thirty (30) days after the casualty, deliver to Tenant Landlord’s good-faith estimate of the time required to complete restoration. Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice given at any time before substantial completion if (a) Landlord’s restoration estimate exceeds one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of casualty, or (b) restoration is not substantially completed within ninety (90) days after the estimated completion date. Upon any such termination, any unearned rent paid in advance shall be refunded and the Security Deposit returned in full. Landlord may terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant if the damage is materially uninsured or occurs during the final twenty-four (24) months of the then-current Term.

original: 15.3  	Data Security.  Each Party shall maintain a written information security program that includes administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the nature and sensitivity of the data processed under this Agreement. In the event of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of research data (a "Security Incident"), the affected Party shall notify the other Party within forty-eight (48) hours of discovering such incident and shall cooperate in investigating and remedying the Security Incident.
revised: 15.3  	Data Security.  Each Party shall maintain a written information security program that includes administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the nature and sensitivity of the data processed under this Agreement. In the event of any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of research data (a "Security Incident"), the affected Party shall (a) provide the other Party with preliminary written notice within seventy-two (72) hours after discovery, identifying the nature of the incident as then understood, the data and systems believed to be affected, a point of contact, and an estimated timeline for investigation, in sufficient detail for the other Party to assess its own regulatory exposure; and (b) provide full written disclosure within seven (7) days after forensic confirmation of the incident’s scope, and shall cooperate in investigating and remedying the Security Incident. Where an incident originates on closed-network hardware or infrastructure that requires physical investigation before its scope can be assessed, the preliminary notice shall so state and shall include the point of contact and estimated timeline, and the seventy-two (72) hour window shall apply to that preliminary notice rather than to the assessment itself. Each Party shall maintain access logs for any monitoring platform, sensor network, or other system of that Party that connects to or collects data from the other Party’s systems, and shall disclose to the other Party in writing, within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date and thereafter within ten (10) business days after discovery, any access event involving the other Party’s systems or data that occurred before the Effective Date or was not logged at the time it occurred. The notification timelines in this Section are intended to support each Party’s obligations under HIPAA and other applicable data protection laws, and nothing herein shall shorten any period required by such laws.
